wageData.title: $30 an Hour is How Much a Year? ($62,400 Salary in 2026)
wageData.metaDescription: $30 an hour is $62,400 per year before taxes, or $5,200/mo and $2,400 biweekly for a 40-hour work week. See exact take-home pay after 2026 taxes.
wageData.h1: $30 an Hour is How Much a Year?
wageData.aeoDirectAnswer: Working 40 hours per week at **$30 an hour** equals an annual gross salary of **$62,400 per year** ($5,200 per month, $2,400 biweekly, or $1,200 per week). After standard 2026 Federal Income Tax ($5,498) and FICA ($4,774), your estimated net take-home pay is approximately **$52,128 per year** ($4,344/month) in zero-income-tax states like Texas or Florida.

faqs.q: $30 an hour is how much a year?
faqs.a: $30 an hour is $62,400 per year for a full-time employee working 40 hours per week (2,080 working hours in 52 weeks). If you take 2 weeks of unpaid vacation (2,000 hours), your annual gross earnings are $60,000.

faqs.q: How much is $30 an hour monthly?
faqs.a: At $30 per hour, your gross monthly pay is approximately $5,200 per month before taxes and deductions.
For employees paid every two weeks (26 paychecks per year), $30 an hour results in a gross biweekly paycheck of $2,400 (80 regular hours).

faqs.q: How much is $30 an hour after taxes?
faqs.a: After subtracting 2026 Federal Income Tax ($5,498) and FICA taxes ($4,774), a single filer takes home approximately $52,128 annually ($4,344/month or $2,005 biweekly) in states with no state income tax. In states like California or New York, state income tax will reduce net pay by an additional $2,496 to $2,808 per year.
